newsitem.title: ESTONIA: BOURSE APPROVES TIGHTER FREE MARKET RULES.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE APPROVES TIGHTER FREE MARKET RULES.

text.p: The Tallinn stock exchange board on Thursday approved tighter requirements for companies listed on the free market, the bourse said.
"Free market companies must publish the information in the same way as companies listed on the stock exchange," Helo Meigas, bourse managing director, told Reuters.
Companies must publish their financial results four times a year and inform of all major changes in their activities.
The stock exchange permits a company to trade on the free market for one year, Meigas said.
During the year, the company must decide whether it wants to have its shares quoted on the official list of the exchange.
Eight companies have to decide during the six months from the date the rules are applied, May 1, Meigas said.
Companies on the free market do not have to pay a listing fee, Meigas said.
Free market companies also do not need to present their official prospectus, she added.
Shares in Tallinna Kaubamaja, Saku Olletehas, Estiko, Eesti Naitused, Norma, EMV, Kalev and Rakvere Lihakombinaat are traded on the Tallinn stock exchange free market.
